model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; GAAP net income after regulatory capital retention, net debt zero)

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is GAAP net income (BAC does not report a separate adjusted 'cash earnings' series the way NAB does): FY2020 $17,894m (COVID provisioning trough) -> FY2021 $31,978m (reserve release) -> FY2022 $27,528m -> FY2023 $26,305m -> FY2024 $26,973m -> FY2025 $30,509m. The 5-year CAGR (11.3%) is inflated by the FY2020 trough and FY2021 reserve-release rebound; the 3-year CAGR from the FY2022 base (3.5%) is closer to trend. Revenue (core_metrics): FY2020 $85,528m -> FY2025 $113,097m.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (7.0% FY27 tapering to 4.0%), anchored between the 3-year (6.0%) and 5-year (5.7%) revenue CAGRs, consistent with management's FY2026 NII guidance (upper end of 6-8%) moderating as trading/IB comparisons normalize and a AAA-rated, GDP-scale loan book cannot compound faster than nominal GDP indefinitely.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.1-3.5%) diverges materially from revenue (5.7-6.0%) and EPS (6.3% 3yr) growth, but for the same reason as NAB/IAG: BAC returns the large majority of earnings via dividends ($0.28/qtr, ~$1.12/yr run-rate) and heavy buybacks ($21.4bn FY2025 alone), so book value is held roughly flat-to-modestly-growing by design rather than compounding with earnings. Growth is taken from the revenue and net-income series, not the equity series.

scenario_narratives.base: BAC grows total revenue 7% in FY2027 as NII keeps ramping on fixed-rate asset repricing and loan growth, fading to 4% terminal as a $3.5tn balance sheet cannot compound faster than nominal GDP forever. Net-income margin improves from ~28% to ~29% as the 300-400bp FY2026 operating-leverage guidance persists via AI/digital cost-out, taking ROE from ~11.5% to ~12.8% mid-cycle. At a 10.5% cost of equity this is worth about 1.35x book (~$56/share) -- close to where BAC already trades (1.37x), meaning the market is pricing this scenario almost exactly, not a re-rating.
scenario_narratives.bull: The September 2026 caution about Q3 investment-banking fees and trading revenue proves overly conservative: Global Markets and Global Banking sustain the H1 2026 boom (record equities, IB fees), NII keeps compounding at the top of guidance, and Basel III Endgame relief frees capital for further growth. Revenue grows 10% fading to 4.5%, ROE reaches 15% on sustained cost discipline, and the franchise is worth ~1.75x book (~$72/share) -- meaningful upside, but it requires several consecutive years of capital-markets strength that BAC's own Q3 guidance says is already decelerating.
scenario_narratives.bear: The yield-curve flattening and credit-cycle risks BAC itself flagged materialize: NII growth stalls well below guidance, the capital-markets slowdown that started with soft Q3 IB/trading guidance persists, and elevated CRE (~$70bn, office-heavy) and card charge-offs rise as the cycle turns. Revenue growth falls to 1.5-2.5%, ROE drops to 8-9.5% (below the cost of equity for most of the projection), and the franchise is worth only ~0.9x book (~$36/share).

valuation_philosophy.summary: A money-center bank holding company is valued on what it can distribute to shareholders after funding regulatory-capital-driven balance-sheet growth, discounted at a USD cost of equity -- never on GAAP operating cash flow (dominated by trading-book and loan-portfolio movements) and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. GAAP net income is the flow; capital retained to fund RWA/balance-sheet growth at the CET1 target is the reinvestment; 10.5% is the return an owner requires given BAC's mix of a sticky deposit franchise and cyclical capital-markets exposure. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at a 12.8% mid-cycle ROE and 4.0% terminal growth the franchise is worth ~1.35x book, almost exactly the 1.37x book the market currently pays -- unlike NAB.AX (market at 2.05x vs. a modeled ~1.4x), BAC is not obviously mispriced on this framework in either direction.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net interest margin and yield curve: FY2026 NII guidance depends on an assumed 25bp September rate cut and continued fixed-rate asset repricing; a flatter curve or fewer cuts than modeled compresses NII directly (BAC_Analysis.json flags this as the highest-severity financial risk)

Capital-markets cyclicality: Q3 2026 guidance of $1.6-1.8bn IB fees (below ~$2bn consensus) and flat trading YoY shows the H1 2026 boom (record equities +70%, IB +50%) can decelerate sharply quarter to quarter; the bear case assumes this persists rather than reverses

Credit cycle: ~$70bn CRE exposure (office-heavy) and elevated card/consumer credit costs are slow-moving overhangs; a recession would raise provisions across consumer and commercial books simultaneously and could push retention needs above the modeled g/ROE relationship

Share count and buyback pace: H1 2026's -5.0% share count decline (7,680.9m -> 7,294.2m) looks opportunistic (buying into the September selloff) rather than sustainable; the model holds shares flat rather than extrapolating that pace, so realized per-share value could be higher if the fast buyback pace continues, or the model could be too generous if it reverts to the slower ~2%/yr historical norm

Book-value basis: no tangible-book/goodwill breakdown was available from the extracted data (pure-XBRL build, no PDFs); BAC carries ~$69bn of goodwill from legacy acquisitions (Merrill Lynch, Countrywide) that GAAP book value does not strip out, so the P/B multiples in this model are on a GAAP-equity basis, not tangible book

Regulatory capital: Basel III Endgame re-proposal (modest system-wide CET1 relief for G-SIBs) is not yet finalized (comments closed June 2026); a stricter-than-modeled outcome would raise retention above the modeled g/ROE and reduce distributable FCFE

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE regular close); 52-week range 46.12-65.23.
data_sources.financials: BAC_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, USD millions, FY2006-FY2025 annual + quarterly through Q2 2026) exported from BAC.duckdb (built via SEC XBRL, no PDFs/Extracted text for this filer); kpis table for buybacks, cash_taxes, ebitda_da.
data_sources.qualitative: BAC_Analysis.json (2026-09-26): business model, competitive position, growth drivers, risk taxonomy, September 2026 guidance/selloff, Q2 2026 earnings detail, bull/bear cases.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total revenue (net interest income + noninterest income), built from H1 2026 actual $61,830m (BAC_Metrics.csv) plus H2 2026E ~$61,145m: Q3 2026E = Q3 2025 actual $28,088m x 1.06 (management guided Q3 IB fees to $1.6-1.8bn, below ~$2bn consensus, and sales & trading roughly flat YoY -- a sharp deceleration from H1's 11% YoY pace, so Q3 growth is held near NII-only run-rate); Q4 2026E = Q4 2025 actual (FY2025 113,097 - H1-2025 55,690 - Q3-2025 28,088 = 29,319) x 1.07 (NII guided to the upper end of 6-8% FY2026 growth, no further trading/IB deceleration assumed). FY2026E revenue of $122,975m is +8.7% YoY vs FY2025's $113,097m, moderating from H1's +11.0% YoY. FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 (just after the valuation date); FY0 = FY2026E puts Year 1 = FY2027, consistent with the engine's end-of-year discounting and the same convention used for NAB.AX/IAG.AX.
inputs.share_count_basis: 7,294.2m shares outstanding at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q, BAC_Metrics.csv), the latest disclosed count. Held FLAT for the engine for the remainder of FY2026 and throughout the projection: BAC's buybacks are a REAL capital-return mechanism (not an SBC-dilution offset as in the owner-FCF convention), and in this FCFE-at-cost-of-equity framework the value of those buybacks is already captured inside the FCFE stream (capital not retained for RWA/balance-sheet growth is, by construction, available for dividends + buybacks) -- flowing it PLUS a declining share count would double-count the same capital return, exactly as NAB.AX's Drivers file holds shares flat despite an active payout policy. Historical count for reference: FY2018 10,236.9m -> FY2025 7,680.9m (-4.0%/yr 7yr CAGR, -2.0%/yr 3yr CAGR); H1 2026 alone saw an unusually fast -5.0% decline (7,680.9m -> 7,294.2m) that looks like opportunistic buying into the September 2026 selloff rather than a sustainable run-rate -- not extrapolated.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction, per the bank/deposit-taker convention (NAB.AX, IAG.AX, SOFI, SRBK precedents). BAC is a bank holding company: customer deposits (~$2.0tn+) and wholesale/long-term debt ($339.9bn at Q2 2026, core_metrics) are operating funding whose cost is already embedded in net interest income; the trading book's balance-sheet assets (securities, loans) are matched by that same funding. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (GAAP net income less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset/balance-sheet growth at BAC's target CET1) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash/securities are added back. total_debt is recorded for audit only; cash_and_equivalents was not populated in core_metrics for FY2021-2025 (large-bank cash/due-from-banks balances are commingled with the trading securities book in BAC's XBRL tags) and is immaterial to this model since net_debt=0 regardless.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = GAAP net income ~$34,187m (revenue $122,975m x 27.8% net margin) less capital retained to fund RWA/balance-sheet growth at the CET1 target (~$5,700m, ~17% of NI at 7% FY27 growth / 11.5% ROE) = ~$28,500m distributable. reported_fcf below is the pre-SBC-charge FCFE proxy so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds (BAC does not report a separate 'cash earnings ex notable items' the way NAB does; there were no large one-off items flagged in FY2025-26 requiring exclusion).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: GAAP operating cash flow is dominated by trading-book and loan-portfolio movements (FY2025 +$12,613m, FY2024 -$8,805m, BAC_Metrics.csv) and is not free cash flow for a bank; reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC add-back, consistent with the NAB.AX/IAG.AX Drivers convention.
inputs.sbc_source: Stock-based compensation $4,200m FY2025, $3,600m FY2024, $3,100m FY2023 (BAC_Metrics.csv, from SEC XBRL cash-flow-statement add-back). H1 2026 SBC $2,150m vs H1 2026 revenue $61,830m = 3.48%; FY2025 was 3.71% of revenue. Modeled path tapers slightly to 3.6% then holds, roughly tracking the recent range.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the core banking business (the single largest revenue line, ~48% of BAC's total per BAC_Analysis.json), and no separate cash balance is added to equity value (net_debt=0 already accounts for this in the other direction, per the bank convention).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buybacks $21,433m (kpis table); Q1 2026 alone $7,240m -- an unusually large, likely opportunistic pace (BAC bought back stock aggressively during the September 2026 bank-stock selloff described in BAC_Analysis.json). Buybacks are the primary distribution channel alongside a $0.28/quarter ($1.12/yr) dividend (Q1-Q2 2026 actual, core_metrics), but per the share_count_basis note above, the VALUE of this capital return is captured inside the FCFE stream at a flat share count, not via a declining share count layered on top.
inputs.book_value_anchor: Total shareholders' equity $301,094m at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q, core_metrics) / 7,294.2m shares = BVPS $41.28. No tangible-book/goodwill breakdown was available in the extracted data for this SEC XBRL-sourced filer (no PDFs/Extracted text; BAC.duckdb built via XBRL), so book value here is GAAP shareholders' equity, not tangible book -- BAC's goodwill (~$69bn, publicly disclosed) is a large, stable balance carried for decades through multiple acquisitions (Merrill Lynch, Countrywide), so the GAAP-book vs tangible-book distinction moves the P/B multiple level but not the FCFE-at-cost-of-equity mechanics, which discount distributable earnings rather than book value directly. Current price $56.70 / BVPS $41.28 = 1.37x book. ROE (H1 2026 annualized net income / average FY2025-Q2 2026 equity) ~11.9%; FY2025 ROE (avg equity) ~10.2%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: US 10-year Treasury ~4.2% (Sept 2026) + beta 1.15 x US equity risk premium 5.5% = ~10.5%. Beta 1.15 reflects BAC's meaningful Global Markets/Global Banking (trading + IB) exposure -- more cyclical than a pure regional bank -- offset by its very large, sticky low-cost deposit franchise, which dampens volatility relative to trading-heavy peers (Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley) or smaller regionals. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle and rate-path risk is charged in the bear flows and the bear probability weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial relative to a $300bn+ equity base and not separately disclosed as a driver in the extracted data; lease cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modeled pretax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are immaterial for BAC (no separate NCI line populated in core_metrics) and are not deducted separately; the effective tax rate driver absorbs any residual leakage.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine, following the NAB.AX (2026-09-24) / IAG.AX (2026-09-23) precedent for the same family (SKILL.md routes banks to 'residual income on tangible book'; FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROE is the clean-surplus equivalent -- FCFE = NPAT x (1 - g/ROE) -- and runs through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook). Engine mapping: revenue = total GAAP revenue (net interest income + noninterest income); ebitda_margin_path = PRETAX margin (net income margin / (1 - effective tax rate)) PLUS SBC% of revenue, matching the NAB convention of adding SBC back before the engine re-subtracts it via sbc_pct_path; effective tax rate assumed at BAC's recent run-rate ~23% (cash_tax_rate_path); da_pct = 0 (BAC does not report a separately add-back-able D&A distinct from noninterest expense; depreciation on premises/equipment/software amortization is a genuine banking cost, not an add-back, matching NAB's treatment); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA/balance-sheet growth at BAC's target CET1 = NPAT margin x g/ROE; wacc = cost of equity 10.5%; net_debt = 0. FY0 reconciliation: revenue $122,975m x (39.96% ebitda margin - 3.6% SBC) x (1 - 23% tax) = ~$34,470m vs the $34,187m NI computed directly from the 27.8% net-margin assumption (small rounding difference from the two-step margin build, immaterial). Residual-income cross-check on GAAP book: P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g); base case terminal ROE 12.8%, g 4.0%, CoE 10.5% -> P/B = 1.35x x BVPS $41.28 = ~$55.9/share, closely matching the engine's discounted-cashflow answer -- unlike NAB (market at 2.05x vs model's implied 1.4x), BAC at 1.37x book is trading close to what this framework says it is worth. Data-source caveat: BAC has no PDFs/Extracted text folder (research/BAC/Extracted/ does not exist) -- this is a pure-XBRL SEC filer build, so all figures are drawn from BAC_Metrics.csv/BAC.duckdb and BAC_Analysis.json rather than page-anchored filing citations; no goodwill/tangible-book or segment-level breakdown was available to refine the book-value anchor beyond GAAP equity.

bear.growth_rationale: The credit and rate risks flagged in BAC_Analysis.json converge: yield-curve flattening and Fed cuts compress NII growth well below guidance, Q3-2026's soft IB/trading guidance ($1.6-1.8bn IB fees, flat trading) proves to be the start of a capital-markets downturn rather than a one-quarter blip, and elevated CRE (~$70bn, office-heavy) and card credit costs rise as the cycle turns. Revenue growth stalls at 1.5-2.5%.
bear.margin_rationale: Net-income margin falls to 24.0% FY27 and 22.0% FY28 (credit provisioning cycle turn, consumer/card and CRE charge-offs rise, operating leverage reverses as revenue stalls but the cost base is stickier), recovering slowly to 24.0% terminal as the bank rightsizes expenses; plus 3.6% SBC add-back.
bear.capex_rationale: ROE falls to 8.0-9.5% (credit cycle turn, below the cost of equity for most of the projection). Retention = NPAT margin x g/ROE stays low (4-6%) because growth itself is weak, not because BAC needs less capital per unit of RWA growth -- in a real downturn (2020 precedent) BAC would likely need to build reserves faster than modeled here, which is why bear is weighted above the house default.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 7.0%: NII still ramping on fixed-rate asset repricing and guided upper end of 6-8% growth, but trading/IB comparisons normalize after H1 2026's outsized 11% YoY revenue growth (record equities +70%, IB fees +50% in Q2 2026 will not repeat). Fades to 4.0% terminal, roughly nominal GDP, consistent with the 3/5-year revenue CAGRs (5.7-6.0%) moderating as a $3.5tn balance sheet cannot keep compounding above-GDP indefinitely.
base.margin_rationale: Pretax margin (net-income margin / (1 - 23% tax)) plus 3.6% SBC add-back. Net-income margin path: 28.0% FY27 (vs FY2026E ~27.8%, FY2025 actual 27.0%, H1-2026 actual 28.6%) rising to 29.0% mid-cycle as the 300-400bp FY2026 operating-leverage guidance persists via continued AI/digital cost-out (300+ approved use cases per BAC_Analysis.json) and held flat thereafter -- BAC's margin has never sustained above ~31% even in strong years, so 29% terminal is not a peak assumption.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to fund RWA/balance-sheet growth at BAC's CET1 target = NPAT margin x g / ROE. ROE path rises from 11.5% (FY27) to 12.8% (mid-cycle, matching H1 2026's already-realized annualized ~11.9% plus continued operating-leverage gains) as the base for retention. At 7.0% growth this retains ~17% of net income (83% distributed via dividends + buybacks); at 4.0% terminal growth only ~9% is retained (91% distributed), consistent with BAC's demonstrated FY2025 payout intensity ($21.4bn buybacks + ~$8bn dividends against $30.5bn net income, ~96% of earnings distributed that year).

bull.growth_rationale: Capital-markets boom continues rather than decelerating in H2 2026: Global Markets and Global Banking sustain record trading/IB revenue (the September 2026 guidance of soft Q3 IB fees proves overly conservative), NII keeps compounding at the top of guidance as deposit/loan growth accelerates, and Basel III Endgame capital relief frees balance-sheet capacity for further loan growth. Revenue grows 10% FY27 fading to 4.5% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: Net-income margin 29.0% FY27 rising to 31.0% mid-cycle as AI/digital productivity gains compound (CTI improves further) and credit costs stay benign; plus 3.6% SBC add-back. 31% would be a multi-year high for BAC but is within reach of JPMorgan's demonstrated efficiency at scale.
bull.capex_rationale: ROE path rises from 12.5% to 15.0% as scale and cost leverage compound; even at a better return, faster growth (10% -> 4.5%) needs more capital retained early (23% of NI at FY27) fading to 9.3% retained at terminal growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 30% and bull cut to 20%: BAC's own September 2026 guidance (Q3 IB fees $1.6-1.8bn below ~$2bn consensus, flat trading YoY) is a live, company-disclosed deceleration signal rather than a hypothetical risk, on top of macro flattening-yield-curve pressure already visible in the September 2026 bank-stock selloff and a slow-moving CRE/card credit overhang. Bull requires the deceleration BAC itself just guided to NOT materialize for a decade, which is a lower-probability path than the house default would suggest.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
